title: "Named character reference state" input consumption
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The [Named character reference state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#named-character-reference-state) of the tokenizer might require further clarification:

It starts off with attempting to match the longest character reference by key in the [spec list](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/named-characters.html). My concern is with the **steps to be taken if there was no match**.

> Otherwise
>    [Flush code points consumed as a character reference](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#flush-code-points-consumed-as-a-character-reference). Switch to the [ambiguous ampersand state](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#ambiguous-ampersand-state).

At this point, it's not clear what has been consumed or put inside the temporary buffer. In my interpretation of the preliminary steps...
> Consume the maximum number of characters possible, where the consumed characters are one of the identifiers in the first column of the [named character references](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/named-characters.html#named-character-references) table. Append each character to the [temporary buffer](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#temporary-buffer) when it's consumed.

... characters are only being consumed (and stored in the temporary buffer) if there's a prefix match for a said sequence from the entity table on the current input position.

When should the tokenizer even consume characters in the "named character reference state"? If it doesn't consume them unless there's a match, there is no point in flushing the buffer on failure (see first quote). If it always consumes characters, when does it have to stop eating the codepoints if there's no well-defined match?
